_comment: Golden wire frames for every frp control message type, as produced by
Every field in pkg/msg/msg.go carries `json:...,omitempty`, so upstream
OMITS zero values. A zero valued Login therefore serialises to `{}`, not
to a long object full of empty strings. That is the single most important
property this corpus pins, and it is the one a hand written encoder is
Each entry pins one frame end to end:
type_byte  - the first byte on the wire, as a character
body       - the exact JSON payload upstream emits
frame_hex  - type_byte || i64 big endian length || body, in hex
note       - why this case is interesting
The bodies were derived from frp v0.71.0's struct tags, and
`regenerate.py` reproduces them by executing frp's own encoder. Run it in
CI to prove the corpus has not drifted.
These vectors exist because the end to end suite cannot see this layer.
A self consistent encoder that emits `subDomain` instead of `subdomain`
keeps both Rust peers talking happily and only breaks against Go. Pin the

vectors.name: login/zero
vectors.note: Every Login field is omitempty, so a zero value serialises to {}. An encoder that emits the full zero filled object is wire wrong, though Go will still decode it.

vectors.name: login/typical
vectors.note: The shape frpc actually sends: only the fields it sets appear, in struct declaration order. metas is an object; client_spec is always present because it is a struct, but its own fields are omitempty so it renders as {}.

vectors.name: login/client_spec
vectors.note: always_auth_pass is omitempty, so it appears only when true. ClientSpec itself has no omitempty, so it is always emitted as at least {}.

vectors.name: login/unicode_metas
vectors.note: Go's encoding/json escapes non ASCII by default, so the metas keys and values are \u sequences rather than raw UTF-8. An encoder that emits raw UTF-8 produces different bytes.

vectors.name: login/empty_metas_map
vectors.note: omitempty drops an empty map, so metas disappears entirely rather than showing as {}.

vectors.name: login_resp/ok
vectors.note: A successful login omits the empty error field.

vectors.name: login_resp/error
vectors.note: Login failure: only error is set.
vectors.body: {"error":"token in login doesn't match token from configuration"}

vectors.name: new_proxy/tcp
vectors.note: Field names are snake_case on the wire while the TOML is camelCase. remote_port is the only non zero field here.

vectors.name: new_proxy/http_vhost
vectors.note: subdomain is the field to watch: the TOML key is subDomain, the wire key is subdomain. custom_domains is a list.

vectors.name: new_proxy/encrypted_compressed
vectors.note: Boolean flags render as true only; a false flag is omitted entirely. bandwidth_limit is carried as its raw string.

vectors.name: new_proxy_resp/ok
vectors.note: remote_addr is a bare port when the bind is on all interfaces, matching net.JoinHostPort semantics.

vectors.name: new_proxy_resp/error
vectors.note: Port already in use is the common failure and must survive the round trip verbatim.

vectors.name: close_proxy
vectors.note: Sent server to client when a proxy is unregistered.

vectors.name: new_work_conn
vectors.note: The privilege key is an md5 hex digest and the timestamp is part of the signed payload.

vectors.name: req_work_conn
vectors.note: An empty struct has no fields at all, so it serialises to {} regardless of omitempty.

vectors.name: start_work_conn
vectors.note: src_port and dst_port are unsigned 16 bit on the wire.

vectors.name: new_visitor_conn
vectors.note: The visitor signature covers run_id, proxy_name, the secret key and the timestamp. The zero valued flags are omitted.

vectors.name: new_visitor_conn/flags
vectors.note: useEncryption and useCompression are negotiated independently for the visitor data path.

vectors.name: new_visitor_conn_resp/ok
vectors.note: The reply to an accepted visitor handshake omits the empty error.

vectors.name: new_visitor_conn_resp/error
vectors.note: A bad sign key is rejected here and must not be silently accepted.
vectors.body: {"proxy_name":"secret","error":"visitor connection request rejected: signature doesn't match"}

vectors.name: ping
vectors.note: Heartbeat from client to server, signed with the same privilege key scheme as login.

vectors.name: pong
vectors.note: An empty Pong serialises to {}; an error would carry text and tell the client the session is dead.

vectors.name: udp_packet/basic
vectors.note: The payload is base64 in key c. local_addr is a net.UDPAddr whose IP marshals as a plain string and whose keys are capitalised.

vectors.name: udp_packet/both_addrs
vectors.note: Both address ends set, which is what the server sends back to the client.

vectors.name: udp_packet/empty_content
vectors.note: A zero length datagram is legal. content is a []byte with omitempty, so an empty slice disappears rather than rendering as an empty base64 string.

vectors.name: nat_hole_visitor
vectors.note: Pre-check negotiation for xtcp. mapped_addrs and assisted_addrs are lists of host:port strings and are omitted when unset.

vectors.name: nat_hole_client
vectors.note: The client half of the hole punch, carrying the sid assigned by the server.

vectors.name: nat_hole_resp
vectors.note: detect_behavior is a nested struct with no omitempty of its own, so it is present whenever it is set; its inner fields are individually omitempty and drop out when zero.

vectors.name: nat_hole_sid
vectors.note: Exchange of the session id between the two clients once the server has paired them.

vectors.name: nat_hole_report
vectors.note: The outcome report that closes a hole punch attempt.
